transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time: 2026-08-12 15:00 PDT; Duration: 52 minutes; Attendees: Aaron Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (CoreVista CTO), Priya Menon (CoreVista SRE), Liam O'Connor (CoreVista Product).

Summary: Quick pacing sync for POC week 3. Focused on capacity sizing for Dedicated pool, autoscale policy tuning, and planning a rehearsal (dry-run) of a scheduled surge. Discussed KV cache priming, prefix caching, and fallback routing to hosted models. Agreed on playbook deliverables and dates.

Topics: capacity numbers, autoscaling thresholds, burst queueing, prefix/K V cache warmup, security questions (KMS, audit logs), next dry-run date.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Aaron (AE): All right, hello everyone, thanks for joining. This is Aaron from Redwood—also have Maya, our SE, on the call. How's everyone doing at CoreVista?
[00:10] Raj (CTO): Hey Aaron, doing good. Busy week but excited to get the rehearsal nailed down.
[00:15] Liam (Product): Hey all. Quick note—we got questions from ops about how Dedicated will behave when we spike to 4x baseline during nightly reports.
[00:25] Maya (SE): Great. Today we want to walk through what we saw in the last run, tune the autoscale policy, and propose the dry-run plan. I'll kick off with a recap of metrics from Friday's test.
[00:38] Maya (SE): So baseline was roughly 120 QPS for model v1. During the scheduled 20-minute surge we pushed to 480 QPS. Observed tail latency creeping to ~520 ms 95th, and we had a smattering of dropped requests—mostly because the burst queue filled and we hit our token-per-minute throttle on the node pool.
[01:05] Priya (SRE): Yeah, and from our side the important piece is those dropped requests map to user-facing errors in the dashboard—so we need graceful degradation or fallback to avoid that.
[01:15] Aaron (AE): Right, fallback was one of the options. We can route to a smaller hosted variant for non-sensitive requests and keep private for PHI. But we need to verify routing rules for that.
[01:28] Raj (CTO): Can you remind me on the routing policy primitives? We can't have PHI leave the VPC for compliance reasons.
[01:35] Maya (SE): Sure. We do policy-level routing: tag requests with data-class, and route by policy. For requests labeled PHI or pii=true we do strict routing to Dedicated only, no fallback. For non-sensitive traffic we can set a fallback to hosted with lower latency SLA. There was a tiny transcription hiccup in our dashboard where 'KV cache' got transcribed as 'K V cash' in logs, but functionally that's the prefix/KV cache.
[02:02] Liam (Product): Ok that helps. On autoscale—what thresholds are we thinking? Last time we had scale-up on 60s windows which felt slow.
[02:12] Maya (SE): Right, current policy uses 60s evaluation window with target utilization 65%. Given the surge shape you described the recommendation is a two-tiered policy: short-window reactive scaler (15s eval, rapid ramp) for up to 2x baseline using predictive step scaling, and then slower warm-scale (2m window) to bring extra instances online for sustained traffic beyond 2x.
[02:40] Priya (SRE): Does that increase cost significantly? We have budget constraints—can't leave extra GPUs idling for hours.
[02:47] Aaron (AE): The cost impact should be modest if you combine predictive warmup with cache priming. The idea is we only warm additional nodes when the curve indicates sustained demand. We'll include an autoscale policy that also has a cooldown and a maximum burst budget per day.
[03:05] Raj (CTO): What's the maximum burst capacity we can reserve in Dedicated? We want guarantee for up to 8x for a 10-minute window if needed.
[03:12] Maya (SE): We can commit to reserved capacity—e.g., keep N reserved GPUs and allow burst to ephemeral nodes up to M additional GPUs, subject to your SLA. But 8x for 10 minutes is doable if you provision a small reserved baseline and allow burst to the shared burst pool—we'll need to check region limits. If it's PHI-regulated, bursts must remain inside the private deployment unless we sign extra agreements.
[03:40] Liam (Product): Can you give a concrete numbers example? Like baseline of 2 GPUs and burst to 8 GPUs—we need to map that to QPS for our model.
[03:48] Maya (SE): Sure. For model v1 on A100-like instance, one GPU gives roughly 80 QPS at 8k tokens average; numbers change with sequence length. So baseline 2 GPUs ≈ 160 QPS, burst to 8 GPUs ≈ 640 QPS. That maps to your observed 480 QPS with headroom. Those are estimates; we'll run a bench to confirm your real QPS per GPU given your token distribution.
[04:20] Raj (CTO): Ok, bench would be great. Last week we saw some cold K V cache penalties—some requests were 1.2x slower until cache warmed.
[04:30] Maya (SE): Yes, prefix caching and KV cache warmup is a big lever. We can seed cache by replaying representative prompts into the system during warmup. For the rehearsal we'll provide a small script to prime popular prefixes so the 95th latency improves quickly during ramp.
[04:47] Aaron (AE): We'll share that script (link: drive.redwood/burst/priming_script.sh) and a short README. Priya, can you run that in staging before the dry-run?
[04:59] Priya (SRE): Yep, we can run it. Need to confirm it won't leak PIIs—it's just synthetic prompts, right?
[05:05] Maya (SE): Exactly synthetic. The script uses obfuscated tokens and dummy PHI markers. We'll document the assertions.
[05:12] Liam (Product): There's also the question of throttling—our app currently retries aggressively which exacerbated queueing last time.
[05:19] Raj (CTO): Right, we should implement backoff and perhaps a soft-404 for non-critical calls.
[05:25] Aaron (AE): Good call. For the rehearsal we recommend client-side retry policy with exponential backoff and a 3rd try max. We'll include suggested code snippets.
[05:34] [06:00] Maya (SE): Quick note—on the private control plane, audit logs are available with per-request metadata. We can feed those to your SIEM. Also, KMS integration is supported; you can bring your own key with HSM. Any questions on encryption?
[06:20] Priya (SRE): Do we get per-request envelopes for logs or just aggregated? We need full per-token audit for compliance.
[06:27] Maya (SE): You can enable per-request audit trails. There is a toggle in the Private control plane. It increases log volume but you get full request/response metadata (note: we mask tokens per your masking policy). We'll include docs.
[06:40] Raj (CTO): Sounds good. One compliance gotcha from legal—they want SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[06:47] Aaron (AE): We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user sync. We'll email the SAML metadata after the call; seeding should be straightforward.
[06:56] Liam (Product): Back to autoscaling—what about queueing strategy? If you have a burst queue, how long do we hold requests before failing?
[07:06] Maya (SE): By default the burst queue holds up to 60s. For your case I'd recommend tightening it to 30s for user-facing paths and longer for batch/async paths. Also we can set priority on routes—critical routes get higher queue weight.
[07:26] Priya (SRE): Can we do differentiated routing by tenant? Some customers are higher SLA than others.
[07:31] Maya (SE): Yes, per-tenant routing and quotas are supported; you can map routes to different pools and apply separate thresholds.
[07:40] Aaron (AE): Ok practical next steps—Maya will produce an autoscale policy yaml with two-step scaling and cost-limits; I'll package the priming script and suggested retry code. We'll run a staged dry-run next Thursday.
[07:55] Raj (CTO): Timeline note—our internal compliance review wraps Monday, so if you can get docs by Friday that helps.
[08:02] Aaron (AE): Noted. Maya, can you call out the exact artifacts and dates?
[08:08] Maya (SE): Yes: 1) Autoscale policy YAML + short explanation (deliver by 2026-08-14). 2) Priming script + README (deliver by 2026-08-14). 3) Short demo showing KV cache warmup and prefix caching behavior (30m video or live) by 2026-08-19.
[08:30] Priya (SRE): We'll run priming script in staging and then run three load profiles: 1) baseline 120 QPS for 30m, 2) ramp to 480 QPS for 20m, 3) spike to 960 QPS for 10m. We'll upload histograms and traces.
[08:48] Maya (SE): Great. For the spike to 960 QPS we may need ephemeral burst nodes and we should test fallback behavior if burst unable to allocate.
[08:58] Liam (Product): On fallback—how will the system choose hosted variant? We need to ensure user experience doesn't degrade too badly.
[09:05] Maya (SE): The routing policy will check data-class and route non-PHI to hosted variant with a lower-cost quantized profile. That reduces quality slightly—quauntization noise—but keeps latency low. We'll show side-by-side outputs in the demo.
[09:25] Raj (CTO): Competitors: we've looked at VendorX and OpenCloud AI. VendorX had simpler autoscale but poor observability. OpenCloud had better burst but not privacy controls.
[09:35] Aaron (AE): Useful context—we'll tailor the playbook to emphasize observability and private-first burst behavior.
[09:40] [30:12] Priya (SRE): A technical question—does the KV cache persist across restarts and model rollouts? We want to avoid cache stampede when we do canary deploys.
[09:52] Maya (SE): Cache is per model-version and stored in memory in the node cluster; we support persisted snapshotting for warm start across restarts and have a cache-grace policy during rollouts to avoid stampede. During canary we route a small percentage and warm cache with synthetic traffic first.
[10:14] Priya (SRE): Nice. That addresses the stampede concern.
[10:20] Aaron (AE): Anything else on the policy yaml? Any knobs we missed?
[10:26] Priya (SRE): Maybe cost ceilings per hour and a circuit breaker that drops to hosted read-only mode if budget threshold hit.
[10:34] Maya (SE): Yes, we can add budget ceilings and a circuit-breaker policy to redirect non-critical routes to hosted. We'll add that to the yaml.
[10:45] Liam (Product): For the rehearsal, we should also simulate client retries to be realistic.
[10:50] Priya (SRE): We'll incorporate that into load generator.
[11:00] Aaron (AE): Ok wrapping up—recap of next steps and owners. Aaron to share playbook links and SAML metadata, Maya to deliver autoscale yaml and demo, Priya and team to run load tests and upload results. Proposed dry-run 2026-08-20 10:00 AM PST.
[11:20] Raj (CTO): That time works for us. We'll confirm calendar invite.
[11:30] Maya (SE): One final note—we recommend running a short benchmark on the exact sequence length distribution you have. If possible, send a sanitized sample of prompts so our bench numbers match reality.
[11:45] Liam (Product): Ok we'll send sanitized sample by EOD Thursday.
[11:50] Aaron (AE): Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts and the calendar hold.
[12:00] Priya (SRE): Thanks. Bye.

Meeting ended 15:52 PDT.

Links referenced: drive.redwood/burst/priming_script.sh, docs.redwood/private-kms-and-audit.md, redwood/playbooks/autoscale-two-step.yaml (draft)

Notes on transcript quality: intermittent mis-transcriptions (e.g., 'K V cash' for 'KV cache', 'quauntization' spelling), some overlapping talk, timestamps approx every 1-2 minutes.
